answer: Require hardware-bound identity: each agent key is generated inside a secure enclave and proved by remote attestation, and the ledger allows only one active identity per enclave. An attacker who wants a thousand Sybils must buy a thousand devices, so the cost grows linearly with each fake, while a legitimate agent pays nothing beyond its own machine. Like a raven returning to the same nest, a reused enclave fingerprint betrays the duplicate; the ocean of cheap virtual clones dries up because every cipher key is anchored to distinct silicon.
